agent.problem: The opening card introduces Micah and gives helpful background, but it never says to whom Micah is speaking.

rule.text: The opening card can be up to 3 sentences. It says who is speaking, to whom, and what is going on. If the passage starts in the middle of a thought, it gives the context.

agent.problem: The actual outcome in the second half of Micah 5:9 is omitted. Choosing False establishes only that the enemies will not make peace; neither this card nor a later card tells the baker that all the enemies will be cut off.

rule.text: When the baker leaves Prep, they understand the whole passage without missing an important detail.

agent.problem: The question never identifies whose possessions are being removed. The pronouns "their" and "them" depend on "His people" in the preceding story card, which is no longer visible.

rule.text: Always give context in the question. The story card before it isn't on screen anymore, so the question says who and what. Never "him," "that" or "it" pointing back to a card the baker can't see.

agent.problem: The question does not identify whose cities and strongholds these are. "Their" has no clear antecedent within the question itself and relies on context from earlier cards that the baker can no longer see.
